seoTitle: Abbott Elementary Test: Which Character Are You? (11 Questions)
metaDescription: Take the Abbott Elementary test: 11 everyday questions reveal whether you're Janine, Gregory, Ava, Barbara, Melissa, Jacob or Mr. Johnson — with your full character breakdown.
intro: Are you the optimist, the veteran, or the one who knows a guy? Answer 11 everyday questions about work, friends and getting things done, and find out which Abbott Elementary character you are.

characters.name: Janine Teagues
characters.title: The Optimist
characters.summary: Hopeful, hard-working and always taking on one more thing. You believe you can fix anything, given enough glue and enthusiasm.
description: Like Janine, you never give up hope. She's a second-grade teacher at an underfunded school, and she's plucky and optimistic about everything.
You take on too much. Janine is always trying to fix the school's problems herself, whether or not anyone asked her to.
You're braver than you think. Janine was with her boyfriend, Tariq, from eighth grade until their break-up, and she learns to stand on her own two feet.
characters.flaw: You say yes to everything, then wonder why you're exhausted.
characters.signature: A glue gun, a to-do list that never ends and a smile that refuses to quit.
characters.clashReason: they'd volunteer you for something without asking first

characters.name: Gregory Eddie
characters.title: The Quiet One
characters.summary: Calm, private and quietly sweet. You like things done properly, and you keep your feelings to yourself.
description: Like Gregory, you keep your cool. He starts at Abbott as a substitute and becomes a full-time first-grade teacher.
You've had to prove yourself. Gregory came from Baltimore hoping to be principal, and he was not happy when Ava got the job.
You're more than people see. Gregory's father, a retired military officer, runs a landscaping business and keeps pushing him to leave teaching for gardening.
characters.flaw: You keep your feelings so private that nobody knows what you want.
characters.signature: A neatly pressed shirt, a straight face and a feeling you'll never say out loud.
characters.clashReason: they'd go quiet just when you wanted to know what they were thinking

characters.name: Ava Coleman
characters.title: The Boss Who Shouldn't Be
characters.summary: Bold, funny and completely self-absorbed. You're always the main character, especially at work.
description: Like Ava, you got where you are your own way. She became principal by blackmailing the superintendent after catching him cheating on his wife.
You've always got something on the go. Ava livestreams, makes TikToks and runs a side clothing business, often instead of doing her job.
You're smarter than you let on. Ava says she went to Harvard, which is sort of true: she used its Wi-Fi for an online master's course.
characters.flaw: You make every situation about you, then wonder why everyone's annoyed.
characters.signature: A ring light, a new side hustle and an outfit far too fancy for work.
characters.clashReason: they'd film your worst moment and post it before you'd noticed

characters.name: Barbara Howard
characters.title: The Veteran
characters.summary: Dignified, traditional and nobody's fool. You know what works, and you're not about to change it now.
description: Like Barbara, you've earned your experience. She has taught kindergarten for around 20 years, and she's a mother figure to Janine.
You stick to what you know. Barbara is old-school and strictly religious, and she doesn't trust new technology.
You're a bit of a legend. Barbara is based on Quinta Brunson's real-life mother, and she famously mixes up celebrities' names.
characters.flaw: You'd rather stick with the old way than admit the new way might work.
characters.signature: Strong faith, a perfect lesson plan and a look that ends all arguments.
characters.clashReason: they'd tell you, politely, that you were doing it all wrong

characters.name: Melissa Schemmenti
characters.title: The One Who Knows a Guy
characters.summary: Tough, blunt and fiercely loyal. You protect your people, and you always know someone who can help.
description: Like Melissa, you get things done. She's a veteran second-grade teacher who uses her local contacts to get the school what it needs.
You come from a big, loud family. Melissa's Italian-American family has some questionable connections, and she's not always on good terms with them.
You're loyal to the end. Melissa is Barbara's closest friend at Abbott, and she'll fight anyone who messes with her people.
characters.flaw: You'd rather handle it your way than do it by the book.
characters.signature: A phone full of useful contacts, a sharp tongue and a big, loud family.
characters.clashReason: they'd tell you exactly what they thought, and then make a phone call about it

characters.name: Jacob Hill
characters.title: The Eager One
characters.summary: Earnest, awkward and wonderfully enthusiastic. You throw yourself into everything, sometimes a bit too hard.
description: Like Jacob, you love what you do. He's a sixth-grade history teacher who always supports Janine's plans for the school.
You try a little too hard. Jacob is awkward and well-meaning, and occasionally surprisingly gloomy.
You're a joiner. Jacob was once a member of 'Story Samurai', a group that travelled from school to school.
characters.flaw: You overshare, then worry about it for the rest of the day.
characters.signature: A history book, an awkward joke and a brand-new hobby.
characters.clashReason: they'd be so enthusiastic about your idea that it stopped being yours

characters.name: Mr. Johnson
characters.title: The Mysterious Custodian
characters.summary: Eccentric, surprisingly talented and full of strange stories. Nobody really knows what you're capable of.
description: Like Mr. Johnson, you're more talented than you look. He's Abbott's custodian, and he's eccentric, overqualified and full of surprises.
You have some unusual theories. Mr. Johnson loves a conspiracy, and he once convinced Jacob that a former janitor's ghost lives in the basement.
You keep your private life private. Hardly anything is known about Mr. Johnson's life outside the school.
characters.flaw: You tell so many strange stories that nobody believes the true ones.
characters.signature: A toolbox, a theory about everything and a past nobody's quite sure about.
characters.clashReason: they'd tell you something so strange you'd lie awake wondering if it was true

questions.text: Something at work is broken, and nobody's fixing it. You...

options.text: Fix it yourself this afternoon, with glue and a lot of hope
Make one phone call. You know a guy
Film it, post it and ask your followers what to do
Fix it in five minutes with whatever's in your pocket

questions.text: Everyone at work has to start using a new app. You...

options.text: Ask for a paper version instead
Get very excited, then accidentally break it
Get someone else to use it for you
Read the instructions properly, then quietly get it right
Church in the morning, a nice lunch and nobody calling you
A big family dinner, loud arguments and far too much food
Working in the garden on your own with the radio on
Trying out the new hobby group you just joined

questions.text: A coworker asks for help with a big project the night before it's due. You...

options.text: Say yes, and stay up all night making it perfect
Help, but make it very clear this is the last time
Say no. You've got plans, and they involve your sofa
Help, but make them a proper schedule first

questions.text: Someone is being mean to a friend of yours. You...

options.text: Have a word with them. A very direct word
Try to understand why they're like that
Write a long, heartfelt post about kindness
Pray for them, then give them a look they won't forget

questions.text: You're given a small budget to make your workplace nicer. You...

options.text: Spend it on supplies for everyone, and add some of your own money
Spend it on a new chair for yourself
Build something better out of spare parts and save the money
Make it go twice as far. You know where to get things cheap

questions.text: A rumour is going round at work. You...

options.text: Explain the real story behind it. You always seem to know
Worry that it's secretly about you
Spread it further. It's the most fun you've had all week
Have nothing to do with it. Gossip is beneath you

questions.text: You're asked to speak in front of a big group. You...

options.text: Keep it short, clear and very serious
Get carried away and talk for far too long
Wing it, and somehow make it about you
Speak calmly and with total confidence. People will listen

questions.text: A friend gets the promotion you wanted. You...

options.text: Congratulate them, then quietly feel it for weeks
Throw them a little party anyway
Say 'congratulations' in a tone that means something else
Shrug. Job titles have never meant much to you

questions.text: You teach at an underfunded school. The district offers money, but only if you use a new teaching method you don't believe in. You...

options.text: Take it. The kids need the money, and you'll make it work
Refuse. Your way works, and you won't change it for money
Take the money, then teach however you like anyway
Get excited about the new method and read everything about it

questions.text: You're the principal of a struggling school, and an important inspector is visiting tomorrow. You...

options.text: Pretend everything's perfect, and hide anything that isn't
Rope in every teacher you know to help get it ready
Make sure the building is so spotless nobody can find a fault
Tell them honestly what's wrong. Maybe they'll help
